classes.name: Voľby do Národnej rady Slovenskej republiky
classes.finest_note: Open data by municipality from 1994 (by district for 1998) and by polling district (okrsok) from 2016; okrsky are lists of streets and are drawn from no published boundary file.
classes.note: 150 seats by list PR (Hagenbach-Bischoff quota and largest remainders), 5% threshold for a party and higher thresholds for coalitions. 1994: four electoral regions (Bratislava and the West, Central, and East Slovak regions) with seats first allocated in each region; one national constituency since 1998 (Act 187/1998, then Act 333/2004 and Act 180/2014). The Slovak National Council elected in 1992 became the National Council on 1 October 1992 under the Constitution. Early elections in 1994, 2006, 2012, 2020 (by date), and 2023 (after the constitutional amendment 91/2023 allowing a shortened term).

cadence.vacancy_rule: A seat falls to the next substitute (náhradník) on the same list by preference order.

classes.finest_note: Open data by municipality from 2004 and by polling district from 2019; 1999 as HTML tables on the office's site.
classes.note: Direct election since the constitutional act 9/1999: a candidate needs a majority of all registered voters in the first round; otherwise the two leading candidates meet in a runoff 14 days later, decided by a plurality of valid votes. Five-year term, at most two consecutive terms. Every direct election so far has gone to a runoff.

cadence.vacancy_rule: A new election is called within seven days and held within 60 days (čl. 101).

classes.name_en: Presidential elections by the National Council
classes.note: Under the original čl. 101 of the Constitution the National Council elected the president by a three-fifths majority by secret ballot: Michal Kováč on 15 February 1993; the 1998 rounds (January to July) elected no one, which led to the direct election of 1999. classes.note: A recall vote is called when three-fifths of the National Council propose it (čl. 106); it removes the President by a majority of all registered voters. None has been held.

classes.name: Voľby do Slovenskej národnej rady
classes.finest_note: 1990 and 1992: the office's HTML pages give list votes and seats by electoral region (volebný kraj).
classes.note: Legislature of the Slovak Socialist (from 1990 Slovak) Republic within the federation. Single-list elections of the National Front in 1971, 1976, 1981, and 1986; in 1990 and 1992 150 seats by list PR in four electoral regions (Act 80/1990), with a 3% threshold in 1990 and 5% in 1992. The council elected in 1992 adopted the Constitution and became the National Council.

classes.name_en: Federal Assembly House of the People elections, in Slovakia
classes.note: Chamber of the Czechoslovak Federal Assembly elected by population. Single lists from 1971 to 1986; in 1990 and 1992 list PR in the four Slovak electoral regions for the Slovak share of its 150 seats (Act 47/1990).

classes.name: Voľby do Snemovne národov Federálneho zhromaždenia (na Slovensku)
classes.name_en: Federal Assembly House of the Nations elections, in Slovakia
classes.note: Chamber of the Federal Assembly with 75 members from each republic (ústavný zákon 143/1968). Single lists from 1971 to 1986; list PR in the four Slovak electoral regions in 1990 and 1992.

classes.name: Voľby do Národného zhromaždenia 1920–1935 (na Slovensku)
classes.name_en: Czechoslovak National Assembly elections, 1920–1935, in Slovakia
classes.note: Chamber of Deputies and Senate of the First Republic, list PR in electoral regions, five of them in Slovakia (Bratislava, Nitra, Turčiansky Svätý Martin, Banská Bystrica, Košice). Elections in 1920, 1925, 1929, and 1935; 1920 voting in the Slovak regions began on 18 April.

classes.name: Voľby do Ústavodarného a Národného zhromaždenia 1946–1964 (na Slovensku)
classes.name_en: Czechoslovak Constituent and National Assembly elections, 1946–1964, in Slovakia
classes.note: The competitive 1946 Constituent Assembly election, then single-list elections in 1948, 1954, 1960, and 1964.
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of the returns for Slovakia was found on volby.statistics.sk or minv.sk; the figures exist only in printed statistical yearbooks and the gazettes of the time.

classes.name: Voľby do Snemu Slovenskej krajiny 1938
classes.name_en: Diet of the Slovak Land election, 1938
classes.note: The autonomous Slovak Land's diet (63 seats) was elected on 18 December 1938 on a single list; it proclaimed the Slovak State on 14 March 1939 and sat until 1945 without a further election.

classes.name: Voľby do Krajinského zastupiteľstva pre Slovensko
classes.name_en: Provincial Assembly of Slovakia elections, 1928 and 1935
classes.note: Two-thirds of the provincial assembly of the Slovak Land were elected by list PR on 2 December 1928 and 26 May 1935, one-third appointed by the government.
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of the returns was found; they are in printed State Statistical Office volumes of the time.

classes.name: Miestne referendum
classes.disposition_reason: Called by municipal councils on mergers, recalling the mayor, or a petition of 30% of voters (§ 11a of Act 369/1990); each municipality announces its own result and no national register of results exists.

classes.name: Voľby do národných výborov
classes.name_en: National committee elections (local, district, and regional), 1954–1986, in Slovakia
classes.note: Single-list elections to the local, town, district, and regional national committees in 1954, 1957, 1960, 1964, 1971, 1976, 1981, and 1986.
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of the returns was found on volby.statistics.sk or minv.sk; only national totals were printed at the time.

classes.name: Obecné a župné voľby 1919–1938
classes.name_en: Municipal and county (župa) elections, 1919–1938, in Slovakia
classes.note: Municipal elections of the First Republic in Slovakia and the elections to the county (župa) assemblies that existed from 1923 to 1928.
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of the returns was found; they are in printed State Statistical Office volumes and municipal records.

classes.name: Nepriame voľby orgánov
classes.name_en: Indirect elections by councils and the National Council
classes.disposition_reason: Officers chosen by elected bodies, not by voters: deputy mayors and boards by municipal councils, deputy regional presidents by regional councils, the Speaker by the National Council, and candidates for the Constitutional Court and the Judicial Council; no electorate votes.

classes.name: Sudcovia
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are appointed by the President on the proposal of the Judicial Council (čl. 145), and Constitutional Court judges by the President from candidates the National Council proposes (čl. 134); none is elected by voters.

classes.name: Rady škôl a školské samosprávne orgány
classes.disposition_reason: School councils are made up of delegates of the founder and of members elected by staff and parents within each school (Act 596/2003); the state runs no public election for them.

classes.name: Výbory v mestských častiach
classes.name_en: Town-part committees outside Bratislava and Košice
classes.disposition_reason: Committees for parts of other towns are set up by the municipal council from councillors elected there and residents it chooses (Act 369/1990); residents do not vote for them.

classes.name: Voľby v profesijných komorách a iných samosprávach
classes.name_en: Elections inside professional chambers, universities, and works councils
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the bodies themselves for their members: professional chambers, university academic senates, and works councils. Slovakia has no elected national minority or other non-territorial public body.

classes.name: Výber kandidátov
classes.disposition_reason: Parties draw up their lists under their own statutes, and independent candidates are nominated by petition; the state runs no primary and publishes no nominating vote.
